title: Spacetime Layout and Logical Compilation of Color Code
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires system-level coordination of logical primitives. Here, we establish a logical compilation framework for the color code, grounded in its topological structure and supporting universal logical operations. Based on its anyon-condensation and domain-wall structure, we introduce a spacetime block-diagram representation capturing logical patches and operations and derive the rules governing block assembly. A correspondence with ZX diagrams further identifies the logical semantics of this representation and enables transformations that preserve the represented computation. Moreover, we develop a code-derived compilation strategy that converts ZX representations of logical computations into valid color-code spacetime layouts. In this strategy, edge-decorated ZX diagrams tailor the logical representation to the color code under the block-assembly constraints, and fusion-region-aware routing exploits semantic equivalence during geometric embedding. We automate the complete logical compilation process and demonstrate successful compilation across a broad range of algorithms. Our work advances color-code architecture from individual primitives to the automated synthesis of logical computations, marking a significant step toward its full-stack quantum computing.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive framework to automate the process of compiling complex quantum algorithms onto the color code. By introducing a spacetime block-diagram representation and linking it to ZX diagrams, the authors provide a systematic method for mapping abstract logical circuits into physical, fault-tolerant lattice layouts. This advances the color code from merely supporting basic gates to enabling full-stack synthesis of arbitrary computations.
main_problem: The goal is to establish a complete, automated logical compilation framework for the color code that supports universal quantum operations.
main_result: The authors developed a systematic method converting abstract ZX diagram representations into valid spacetime layouts on the color code lattice, achieving automated synthesis of complex computations.
method: They introduce a novel 'spacetime block-diagram representation' and derive assembly rules connecting it to existing semantic tools like edge-decorated ZX diagrams for compilation.
model_or_system: The system is the 2D color code implemented on a hexagonal (6.6.6) lattice, which encodes logical qubits using topological structures defined by anyons and domain walls.
key_observables: Logical Pauli operators ($	ext{X}, 	ext{Z}$), spacetime volume, degree of junctions (up to five).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the ability to map logical operations onto the color code's topological structure and relies on established correspondences with ZX diagrams.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate anyon types, stabilizer structures per face, spacetime building blocks (Prism, Time Pipe, Space Pipe), and how logical operators deform across high-degree junctions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the color code's topological features to introducing the spacetime block diagram representation, establishing its correspondence with ZX diagrams, and finally developing the automated compilation strategy for universal gates.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract computation, the rigorous geometric mapping of logical operations onto a physical lattice structure provides deep insights into how topological constraints govern quantum information processing architectures.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Left: The anyons in the color code. A string of physical X operators supported on a path connecting two red faces creates a pair of rx anyons at those faces. A single physical Z operator creates a triple of anyons rz, gz, and bz at the three faces adjacent to the qubit. Middle: The stabilizers of the color code. Each face hosts two stabilizers, one in the X basis and one in the Z basis. Right: A triangular patch of the 2D color code, with its three colour boundaries and logical operators. The logical Pauli operators can either be represented as star-shaped string operators in the bulk or as line operators along the boundaries.

Figure 2: The building blocks of the spacetime layout of the 2D color code. Left: a prism, with its top and bottom faces as Pauli X boundaries and its lateral faces as colour boundaries. Middle left: a time pipe, with a transparent domain wall carrying a sequence of single-qubit Clifford gates. Middle right: a space pipe, with its top and bottom faces as blue colour boundaries and its lateral faces as Pauli Z boundaries. Right: a magic state injection port (purple), which is attached to a junction. A magic state is injected asynchronously at the port.
Figure 3: Left: All possible z-basis junctions of degree 2, 3, 4, and 5 in the spacetime layout of the 2D color code. Right: The corresponding ZX diagram of each junction.

Figure 4: Left: Two prisms with deferred basis in the spatial direction, and the corresponding rep- resentation in ZX diagram. Right: One prism with deferred basis in the temporal direction, and the corresponding representation in ZX diagram.
Figure 5: The result of our compilation pipeline for the 16-qubit VQE circuit. Left: the compiled spacetime layout. Right: the corresponding ZX diagram.
